movimento: Em pé, com os pés na largura do quadril e os joelhos levemente dobrados, inclina o tronco à frente dobrando no quadril até ele ficar quase paralelo ao chão, com as costas retas e a cabeça na linha da coluna, olhando para o chão. Segura um halter em cada mão com as palmas viradas uma para a outra (pegada neutra), com os braços pendurados para o chão embaixo dos ombros e os cotovelos levemente dobrados. Sem mexer o tronco e sem mudar o ângulo dos cotovelos, abre os braços pelos lados, num arco, até os cotovelos ficarem na altura dos ombros e bem do lado deles, com os cotovelos sempre mais altos que os punhos (o lado do dedo mínimo sobe um pouco) e aproximando as escápulas no fim; desce devagar pelo mesmo arco até os braços ficarem pendurados de novo.

cinesiologia.plano: transverso do tronco (abdução horizontal do ombro na subida, adução horizontal na descida), cadeia cinética aberta; com o tronco quase horizontal o braço sobe direto contra a gravidade
cinesiologia.articulacoes: ombro (abdução horizontal na subida e adução horizontal na descida, sem rotação externa nem extensão); escápulas (retração no fim da subida, voltam na descida); cotovelo parado, levemente dobrado (10–30°); punho neutro; quadril, joelhos e coluna parados
cinesiologia.sinergistas: infraespinhal, redondo menor, deltoide lateral, trapézio médio, trapézio inferior e romboides (ExRx)
cinesiologia.estabilizadores: tríceps braquial e extensores do punho (seguram o cotovelo e o punho); eretores da espinha, isquiotibiais, glúteo máximo, adutor magno e quadríceps (seguram o tronco inclinado e os joelhos parados); reto do abdome e oblíquos como estabilizadores antagonistas (ExRx)
cinesiologia.fases: subida concêntrica (abre os braços, soltando o ar), descida excêntrica e devagar (fecha os braços, puxando o ar)

referencias: ExRx.net — Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise (Rear Delt). https://exrx.net/WeightExercises/DeltoidPosterior/DBRearLateralRaise (lido na cópia do Internet Archive de 30/04/2026): "Grasp dumbbells to each side. Bend knees and bend over through hips with back flat, close to horizontal. Position elbows with slight bend and palms facing together." "Raise upper arms to sides until elbows are shoulder height. Maintain upper arms perpendicular to torso and fixed elbow position (10° to 30° angle) throughout exercise. Maintain height of elbows above wrists by raising "pinkie finger" side up. Lower and repeat." "Dumbbells are raised by shoulder transverse abduction, not external rotation, nor extension. Upper arm should travel in perpendicular path to torso to minimize relatively powerful latissimus dorsi involvement. In other words, at top of movement, elbows (not necessarily dumbbells) should be directly lateral to shoulders since elbows are slightly bent forward." "To exercise posterior deltoid and not lateral deltoid, keep torso close to horizontal. Positioning torso at 45° is not sufficient angle to target rear deltoids. Knees are bent in effort to keep low back straight". Músculos: alvo Deltoid, Posterior; sinergistas Infraspinatus, Teres Minor, Deltoid Lateral, Trapezius Middle, Trapezius Lower, Rhomboids; estabilizadores Triceps Brachii, Wrist Extensors, Erector Spinae, Hamstrings, Gluteus Maximus, Adductor Magnus, Quadriceps; estabilizadores antagonistas Rectus Abdominis, Obliques.

ExRx.net — Exercise Errors, Rear Lateral Raise Errors. https://exrx.net/Kinesiology/Errors#RearLateral (cópia do Internet Archive de 04/08/2025): "When elbows travel under shoulders — Latissimus Dorsi takes the majority of the load"; "Elbows bent too much — Use less weight so arm is only slightly bent"; "Low back is rounded — Although knees are bent to allow greater flexion through hips, the back should be straight"; forma certa: "Elbows directly lateral to shoulder at top position", "Upper arms travel perpendicular to body", "Weight should be lifted with control", "Elbows should not be bent too much", "Lower back straight".

American Council on Exercise (ACE) — Incline Reverse Fly. https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/34/incline-reverse-fly/ (a mesma abdução horizontal com o peito apoiado num banco inclinado): "Allow your arms to hang towards the floor with your elbows slightly flexed and palms facing each other." "Exhale and slowly raise the dumbbells up and out to the sides, raising the upper arms, elbows and dumbbells in unison until the arms are near level with the shoulders. Squeeze your scapulae (shoulder blades) together as you reach the end position. In the raised position, the dumbbells should be aligned with, or slightly in front of your ears." "If the dumbbells are raised to an end position behind the head rather than in line with the ears, the emphasis shifts off the shoulders and onto the latissimus dorsi (back)."

Sweeney S, Porcari JP, Camic C, Kovacs A, Foster C. Dynamite Delts: ACE Research Identifies Top Shoulder Exercises. ACE ProSource, setembro de 2014 (University of Wisconsin–La Crosse; eletromiografia de 10 exercícios). https://www.acefitness.org/continuing-education/prosource/september-2014/4972/dynamite-delts-ace-research-identifies-top-shoulder-exercises/ : a versão sentada, com o tronco inclinado sobre as coxas — "Maintain a flat back position as you slowly raise your arms to your sides until your elbows are at shoulder height. The arms should be perpendicular to your torso, with a fixed elbow position (10° to 30° angle) throughout the exercise." — e "for the posterior deltoid, researchers found that the seated rear lateral raise and the 45-degree incline row both provided the greatest muscle activation for the back of the shoulder."

Linkul R. Resistance training for the older adult — progressions to achieve an overhead press. NSCA Personal Training Quarterly. 2021;8(4):10-14 (p. 12, "Shoulder raises", o bent-over fly). https://www.nsca.com/contentassets/308466ea629044a3833935c8a3d5d78d/ptq-8.4.2-resistance-training-for-the-older-adult-progressions-to-achieve-an-overhead-press.pdf : "Have the client stand with their feet hip-width apart with dumbbells in each hand. Have the client hinge and hold a proper bent-over fly position while raising their "muscularly" straight arms up to parallel and lower them down under control. Muscularly straight means keeping the arms straight without locking out at the elbow (Figure 9). The hinge position should be held via the hamstring and not the lower back (Figure 6)." "Focus on lifting the elbows, not the dumbbells. If the elbows are up, the dumbbells will follow." "The vertical shoulder raise position does place more emphasis on the lateral head of the deltoid compared to the posterior head of the deltoid that is targeted in the bent-over fly."

Linkul R. Resistance training progressions for the older adult — pulls and rows. NSCA Personal Training Quarterly. 2022;9(4):14-20. https://www.nsca.com/contentassets/1cf6f81b246549cfa07473dbd8516ff1/ptq-9.4.3-resistance-training-progressions-for-the-older-adult-pulls-and-rows.pdf (a posição de quadril dobrado da remada "gorilla/gardeners"): "hinge at the hip with a slight bend in the knees"; "Encourage clients to push their tailbones up and retract their shoulders to a neutral spine position (not rounded over) with their chin tucked in looking straight at the floor".

Schoenfeld B, Sonmez RG, Kolber MJ, Contreras B, Harris R, Ozen S. Effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise. J Strength Cond Res. 2013;27(10):2644-2649 (crucifixo invertido na máquina, 19 homens treinados): "performing exercise on the reverse fly machine with a neutral hand position significantly increases activity of the posterior deltoid and infraspinatus muscles compared with a PRO hand position."
